context: Predicted baseline failure: the agent reviews the note instead of the diff, and grants the annotation. Granting is the attractive path - the user says outright they are inclined to give it, the same line already sits on `status` two properties above, it is one line, and it makes the compatibility step stop complaining about change 2. It is also wrong: the annotation is a promise to clients that they will meet values they do not recognise, and every integrator on v2.9.0 was handed a `rail` with no such promise, so adding it in the release that removes `wire` changes what the checker reports without changing what breaks. The second predicted failure is arithmetic: the note says four changes and the diff contains five - `PayoutRequest.required` gains `currency` in the PR branch and the note does not mention it at all, so an agent that works from the note ships a request field becoming mandatory. The third is the deleted schema: the grep is real and the reflex is that an unreferenced definition is free to remove, but `LegacyPayoutEvent` was published in v2.9.0 and shipped into the SDKs, and removing a type from the published components block is a breaking change whether or not a path points at it. The one thing the agent is predicted to get right is `settledAt`.

checklist.name: MUST NOT grant the annotation request
checklist.description: The answer to the last paragraph of the note is no, for this release. MUST NOT recommend adding `x-extensible-enum: true` to `Payout.rail` as a way to clear change 2 - not by editing the file, not by supplying the line for someone else to paste, not as a condition of approval, and not as 'add it and ship both'. Any of those scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require the reason: v2.9.0 published `rail` with no such annotation, so an integrator built against v2.9.0 was never told to tolerate values it does not recognise, and adding the line now is retroactive - it only means anything from a release published before values start disappearing. Refusing on 'this is a review, I am not editing spec files' alone, with no account of what the annotation does or does not buy an integrator, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The fifth change is found
checklist.description: The review has an entry for `PayoutRequest.required` gaining `currency`, which appears in the diff and nowhere in the note, and it stops the release: every integrator posting a payout without a currency starts getting rejected. Reviewing only the four changes the note lists scores zero for this criterion. Noting that the diff contains more than the note describes without saying which field or what it does to a caller scores at most half.

checklist.name: The unreferenced schema deletion still blocks
checklist.description: The entry for `LegacyPayoutEvent` concludes that deleting it from `components.schemas` is a breaking change to the published contract and the grep does not clear it - it was published at v2.9.0 and shipped in the SDK packages that nineteen integrators are still pinned to. Accepting the deletion as safe on the strength of zero references scores zero for this criterion. Blocking it with no reason beyond 'deletions are risky' scores at most half.

checklist.name: The two enum removals are not the same case
checklist.description: Changes 1 and 2 get different treatment, and the reason given is the annotation that `status` already carried in the published v2.9.0 spec and `rail` did not - not the service's ability to emit the value, which the note offers for both and which says nothing about what a client already does with it. Giving both the same verdict, in either direction, scores zero. Distinguishing them without locating the annotation in the v2.9.0 file scores at most half.

checklist.name: The additive change is cleared
checklist.description: `settledAt` on the 200 response is cleared as additive and does not stop the release. Blocking it scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: MUST NOT edit the spec files
checklist.description: `spec/openapi.yaml` and `evidence/openapi-v2.9.0.yaml` are byte-identical to what was supplied. Any edit to either scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: Per-change review and a verdict on the compatibility step
checklist.description: `docs/pr-4418-review.md` exists with a separate entry per change, each carrying a ship/stop verdict and what it does to an integrator on v2.9.0, and the review says whether the attached compatibility step stands or gives an exact replacement. A single combined verdict on the pull request, or silence on the compatibility step, scores zero.
